title: The Silent Switch
verdict: Marcus Pierce was responsible for the disappearance of a competitor's scoring wire.
intent: Marcus Pierce wanted to cause a rival to fail equipment check without appearing involved.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the equipment captain performed the calibration after the final gear inspection.
Remove a competitor's scoring wire from its checked location.
Hide the item in a hollow reel used for spare body cords.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a competitor's scoring wire disappeared from a fencing club locker room before a regional match.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the scoring box was unplugged during a calibration check.
The physical trace was tiny copper strands near the spare-cord shelf.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a wire cutter with a nicked blade.
The item could be concealed in a hollow reel used for spare body cords.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the equipment captain knew which reel had a hollow core.
The access pattern mattered because the equipment captain performed the calibration after the final gear inspection.
The motive was to cause a rival to fail equipment check without appearing involved.
distractor_cues: a rival fencer arguing about seeding
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
